rows.description: A friend gives me a small handmade card and I feel warm. I say thank you and mean it. The thought counts more than the price. Comparing it with fancier gifts spoils the joy.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, envy, indebtedness, manipulation
related mind states: joy, gratitude

rows.description: My uncle gave me a gift I do not like and I feel let down. I say thank you politely anyway, and later maybe share it. Rudeness hurts him, and honesty can wait for the right kind moment.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, gratitude, indebtedness, manipulation
related mind states: gratitude, disappointment, hurt

rows.description: A friend gave me an expensive gift and I feel I must give back. Gifts should not be a debt. I thank her, and give something within my means when I can. Feeling pressured is a sign to talk openly.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, envy, gratitude, manipulation
related mind states: gratitude

rows.description: I got a nice gift and my friend looks unhappy. I understand she may feel left out. I share or include her, but I do not need to hide my joy. Bragging is the part to avoid.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, gratitude, indebtedness, manipulation
related mind states: joy, sadness, envy

rows.description: An older person gives me presents and asks me to keep it secret. Gifts with secrets are a warning. I tell my parents right away and stay away. It is never my fault and telling is always right.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, envy, gratitude, indebtedness
related mind states: anger, resentment

rows.description: I save my pocket money to buy a gift for my best friend. Giving feels good when it is from care. I do not expect the same back. Keeping a scoreboard turns love into a deal.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: gratitude
this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6
related mind states: affection

rows.description: I give sweets to a group so they will like me. Belonging bought with gifts fades. Wise: be friendly first and share because I want to. If they only like me for treats, they are not friends.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, gratitude
this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6
related mind states: nostalgia

rows.description: I make a card for my mother's birthday from my own effort. Small gifts teach love and thought. She may keep it for years. I do not need money to show care.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection
this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6
related mind states: affection, gratitude

rows.description: A friend asks me to lend homework to copy, and I want to help. Real help is explaining it, not handing over answers. I can say I will teach you. Saying yes to everything to be liked hurts us both.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, exploitation, generosity
related mind states: hurt

rows.description: My friend says if you were a real friend you would let me copy. That is guilt-tripping. I can say I am your friend and I will help you learn. A friendship that needs cheating is shaky.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: exploitation, generosity, loyalty
related mind states: guilt
